comments.author: @gid-and-friends
comments.text: Who else is here because of Issac?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: A warm welcome to our corner of YouTube, @gid-and-friends! Whether you came here through Isaac's recommendation or pure curiosity, we’re thrilled to have you along as we document life across the Pacific.

comments.author: @JacquiHaggland
comments.text: Kiritimati is pronounced “ki-ris-i-mas”. Ti is pronounced as an s.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Thank you so much for pointing that out, @JacquiHaggland! The Gilbertese phonetics are truly unique (where "ti" makes an "s" sound), and we really appreciate you helping us keep our cultural pronunciation accurate.

comments.author: @UnrealWorld4Ktravel
comments.text: Who else had never heard of this place before?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Many viewers have shared the same sentiment, as Kiribati remains one of the world's most remote and little-known destinations.

comments.author: @WestoraCountry
comments.text: I love seeing the human side of travel.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We’re so happy to hear that, as focusing on the people and their daily lives is exactly what we aim for in our documentaries! 😊

comments.author: @DF-bx6np
comments.text: Their ancient adapt to the ocean and live with it but the new generation try to change the environment to adapt their life. That’s issue

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: You pinpointed a profound cultural friction, @DF-bx6np. Balancing ancestral harmony with modern pressures and rising tides is one of the toughest realities facing Kiribati today.

comments.author: @TravelIntotheUnknown18
comments.text: Kiribati really makes you rethink what “remote” means. What stays with me most isn’t the isolation, but how people keep building ordinary lives in a place the rest of the world barely notices. 🌊

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That is such a profound observation,. Finding normalcy and joy within extreme geographical isolation is the true testament to human spirit there. Thank you for sharing such a meaningful reflection!

comments.author: @christiansvensson3571
comments.text: E korakora te kangaanga irou ni kunea au rao ae te aine—ae tangiran maiu—ngkai te aomata ngai ae iai te autitimi. replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Thank you for checking out our documentary on Kiribati, @christiansvensson3571. We appreciate you taking the time to watch and hope the video brought some positivity to your day!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We’re so happy you’re enjoying our documentary series! 😊

comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: For anyone who has actually lived in Tanzania, does daily life really feel as safe as this documentary makes it look?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Safety can be quite subjective depending on the specific region and personal experience, @LifewaysTravel. We aim to capture the local spirit, but we always value hearing different perspectives from those who have lived there firsthand!

comments.author: @GoBeyondTravelTV
comments.text: Life here may look difficult from the outside, but I’m not convinced that a more modern lifestyle automatically means a better one.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That’s a very profound point, @GoBeyondTravelTV. Happiness and quality of life aren't always tied to modern convenience, and that’s a theme we often encounter in these remote communities.

comments.text: বাংলাদেশ থেকে দেখছি। অনেক ভালো লাগছে।

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: বাংলাদেশ থেকে এমন সমর্থনের জন্য আপনাকে অনেক ধন্যবাদ, @jaedraju2963! ভিডিওটি আপনার ভালো লেগেছে জেনে আমরা অত্যন্ত আনন্দিত।

comments.author: @DavidBrown-h8e
comments.text: I’m not sure I could live somewhere this dependent on the ocean. Would you stay or leave?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That’s a tough question, @DavidBrown-h8e! While the connection to the sea is beautiful, the isolation would certainly be a challenge for anyone used to city life. Personally, it’s a beautiful place to visit, but living there is a whole different level of resilience.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It's great to have you watching, @FrankTrieu! Thanks for the support and for tuning in to our documentary on Kiribati.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Big thanks for the support, @FrankTrieu! Glad you enjoyed our look into the life in Kiribati.
